papers.title: Multi-Omics-Guided Discovery of Holothuria scabra-Derived Drug Candidates Targeting Ferroptosis and the Bone Tumor Microenvironment in Osteosarcoma.
papers.abstract: Osteosarcoma remains the most common primary malignant bone tumor in adolescents and is characterized by aggressive metastasis, resistance to therapy, and extensive bone microenvironment remodeling. Therefore, the identification of novel multi-target therapeutic agents capable of simultaneously inducing ferroptosis and disrupting tumor-supportive signaling is urgently needed. This study employed a multi-omics-guided approach to investigate the anti-osteosarcoma potential of metabolites derived from the sea cucumber Holothuria scabra. LC-MS/MS profiling identified major bioactive constituents,
papers.summary: This study used a multi-omics approach to identify compounds from sea cucumber Holothuria scabra that could target ferroptosis and the bone tumor microenvironment in osteosarcoma. LC-MS/MS profiling revealed key bioactive metabolites with potential as multi-target therapeutic agents.

papers.title: MPLID (Membrane Protein-Lipid Interaction Database): A Large-Scale Experimental Resource of Residue-Level Protein-Lipid Contacts.
papers.abstract: Membrane proteins constitute approximately 20-30% of all proteomes and represent over 60% of current drug targets. Although protein-lipid interactions play important structural and regulatory roles in membrane-associated proteins, most existing structural resources focus on identifying whether a residue lies within a membrane region, typically inferred from computational hydrophobicity-based positioning algorithms. This approach does not directly address a distinct biological question: which residues at the protein surface make direct physical contact with lipid molecules? Answering this quest
papers.summary: The authors present MPLID, a large-scale database that experimentally identifies which residues on membrane proteins directly contact lipid molecules, moving beyond computational predictions of membrane region location. This resource addresses a key gap in understanding the structural and regulatory roles of protein-lipid interactions, which are critical for over 60% of drug targets.

papers.title: First Report of (E)-1-Phenyl-3,7-dimethyl-2-octen-1-ol and N-propyl-4-methoxycinnamamide from Aegle marmelos unripe fruit: Isolation, characterization and mechanistic evaluation of proton pump inhibitory and antioxidant activities.
papers.abstract: Aegle marmelos (L.) Corr. (Rutaceae) is a medicinally important tree widely used across South Asia for the treatment of gastrointestinal disorders including peptic ulcers, diarrhea, and dysentery. Beyond its antiulcer applications, the plant has been reported to possess antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and cytoprotective activities. However, the specific bioactive compounds and mechanisms underlying proton pump inhibition remain insufficiently characterized at the molecular level.To isolate and characterize bioactive constituents from the unripe fruit of A. marmelos responsible f
papers.summary: This study isolated two new compounds from unripe Aegle marmelos fruit and showed they inhibit proton pumps and have antioxidant activity, providing a molecular basis for the plant's traditional use against ulcers.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics analysis suggests a potential mechanism of DEHP-induced monocyte infiltration in MASH via the FOS-CCL3/4 axis.
papers.abstract: Di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) is a widespread environmental obesogen; however, its immune-proinflammatory mechanisms in the progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) remain incompletely elucidated. This study aims to comprehensively characterize the core targets and molecular mechanisms by which DEHP disrupts the hepatic microenvironment and drives disease progression through multi-omics integration and experimental analysis.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the environmental chemical DEHP contributes to liver inflammation in MASH by integrating multi-omics data. The authors identify that DEHP promotes monocyte infiltration into the liver through the FOS-CCL3/4 signaling axis, revealing a potential immune mechanism linking environmental exposure to disease progression.

papers.title: BBP acts as an exogenous modulator of MMP9 to rewire vascular immunity and promote atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: Environmental exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals has been increasingly implicated in cardiovascular disease, yet the causal molecular mechanisms linking such exposures to atherosclerosis remain incompletely defined. Benzyl butyl phthalate (BBP), a widely used plasticizer, has been associated with vascular dysfunction, but its mechanistic contribution to atherogenesis is unclear. Here, we employed an integrative systems biology framework combining network toxicology, transcriptomic profiling, protein-protein interaction network analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations
papers.summary: This study identifies benzyl butyl phthalate (BBP), a common plasticizer, as an exogenous modulator of MMP9 that rewires vascular immunity and promotes atherosclerosis. Using an integrative systems biology approach, the authors elucidate a causal molecular mechanism linking this environmental chemical to cardiovascular disease.

papers.title: Comprehensive analysis of the molecular dynamics of bisphenol compounds and prediction of their effects on prostate cancer progression.
papers.abstract: Bisphenols are a class of widely occurring environmental endocrine disruptors, but a comprehensive understanding of their systemic effects on prostate cancer progression under conditions of low-concentration exposure remains lacking. This study established a comprehensive research framework integrating bioinformatics analysis, functional experiments, and structural biology analysis to systematically evaluate the cancer-promoting effects of eight bisphenol compounds, namely, BPA, BPAF, BPB, BPC, BPE, BPF, BPS, and BPZ, in prostate cancer. Enrichment analysis revealed that, across cancer types,
papers.summary: This study integrates bioinformatics, functional experiments, and structural biology to evaluate how eight bisphenol compounds (including BPA and BPS) promote prostate cancer progression, even at low concentrations. Enrichment analysis across cancer types reveals shared cancer-promoting pathways, providing a comprehensive framework for understanding the endocrine-disrupting effects of bisphenols.

papers.title: Computational mapping of productive POI-E3 ligase conformations to guide de novo degrader design: application to WEE1 and PKMYT1 PROTACs.
papers.abstract: Targeted protein degradation has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy, yet rational degrader design remains challenged by the dynamic nature of protein of interest (POI)-E3 ligase interactions. While X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM provide valuable structural snapshots, they are insufficient for capturing the conformational heterogeneity underpinning efficient ubiquitination and degradation. Here, we present a unified computational workflow to systematically generate and evaluate POI-E3 ligase conformational states for CRBN- and VHL-mediated proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs). T
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational workflow to model the dynamic conformations of protein-of-interest (POI) and E3 ligase complexes, addressing a key challenge in designing PROTAC degraders. The method was applied to WEE1 and PKMYT1 targets, enabling more rational degrader design by predicting productive conformations for ubiquitination.

papers.title: Structural and functional effects of carbonylation and phosphorylation on the Zu5-ANK domain: A molecular dynamics and docking study.
papers.abstract: 4-HNE carbonylation and phosphorylation in the Zu5-ANK domain have been observed in human erythrocytes with sickle cell trait and G6PD deficiency. However, the atomic-level effects of phosphorylation and multiple carbonylations by 4-HNE on the Zu5-ANK domain are not yet fully understood. The present work provides further insight into understanding the changes caused by polymodifications in Zu5-ANK due to oxidative stress and phosphorylation. Here, we present a molecular dynamics simulation-based study of the polycarbonylated, phosphorylated, and phosphocarbonylated Zu5-ANK domain. Our results
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how carbonylation and phosphorylation modifications alter the structure and function of the Zu5-ANK domain, which is relevant to sickle cell trait and G6PD deficiency. The findings provide atomic-level insights into how these post-translational modifications, induced by oxidative stress, affect protein behavior.

papers.title: Antidiabetic potential of a novel hydroxyphenyl-bi-benzopyran-hexol compound from Cassia fistula as an α-amylase inhibitor: Integrated in silico screening and in vitro validation using a nonlinear regression model.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a critically important metabolic disease, causing persistent hyperglycemia. Blood glucose levels can be effectively maintained by inhibiting the activity of α-amylase. α-amylase inhibitors manage postprandial hyperglycemia by delaying carbohydrate digestion.
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
papers.summary: This study identifies a novel compound from Cassia fistula that inhibits α-amylase, an enzyme involved in carbohydrate digestion, suggesting potential as a natural antidiabetic agent. The authors used computational screening and in vitro experiments with a nonlinear regression model to validate the compound's activity.

papers.title: Integrated computational and experimental evidence of biochemical and physiological perturbations induced by environmentally relevant thallium exposure in Daphnia magna.
papers.abstract: Thallium (Tl), a highly toxic heavy metal, poses a serious threat to freshwater ecosystems. This study investigated the chronic toxicity of Tl(I) in Daphnia magna using an integrated approach combining network toxicology, molecular docking, and biochemical assays. Network analysis identified 23 candidate enzyme targets, with significant enrichment in pathways related to glutathione metabolism, suggesting a potential involvement of antioxidant regulation in Tl(I)-induced toxicity. Molecular docking indicated energetically favorable spatial associations between Tl(I) and several enzymes, suggest
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated approach combining computational modeling and wet-lab experiments to show that environmentally relevant levels of thallium disrupt glutathione metabolism and antioxidant pathways in Daphnia magna, providing mechanistic insight into its chronic toxicity in freshwater ecosystems.

papers.title: Benchmarking sequence-based and AlphaFold-based methods for pMHC-II binding core prediction: distinct strengths and consensus approaches.
papers.abstract: Interactions between peptide and MHC class II (pMHC-II) are crucial for T-cell recognition and immune responses, as MHC-II molecules present peptide fragments to T cells, enabling the distinction between self and non-self antigens. Accurately predicting the pMHC-II binding core is particularly important because it provides insights into pMHC-II interactions and T-cell receptor engagement. Given the high polymorphism and peptide-binding promiscuity of MHC-II molecules, computational prediction methods are essential for understanding pMHC-II interactions. While sequence-based methods are widely
papers.summary: This study benchmarks sequence-based and AlphaFold-based methods for predicting the binding core of peptides to MHC class II molecules, finding that each approach has distinct strengths. The authors propose that combining these methods into a consensus approach may improve prediction accuracy, which is important for understanding immune responses and T-cell recognition.

papers.title: Atomistic Insights into Graphene Oxide Dot Interactions with Integrin αVβ3 from Microsecond Simulations.
papers.abstract: Graphene oxide (GO)-based nanomaterials functionalized with targeting ligands are promising platforms for selective cancer drug delivery. Among relevant targets, integrin αVβ3 is a highly overexpressed receptor in several solid tumors and is commonly targeted using cyclic Arg-Gly-Asp (cRGD) peptides. However, the molecular details governing the interaction between cRGD-functionalized GO dots and integrins remain poorly understood. In this work, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations are employed to investigate the interaction between integrin αVβ3 and a nanocarrier composed of a GO dot coated
papers.summary: This study uses all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to reveal how graphene oxide dots functionalized with cRGD peptides interact with the integrin αVβ3 receptor, a key target in cancer drug delivery. The simulations provide atomistic details of the binding mechanism, which could inform the design of more effective nanocarriers for selective cancer therapy.

papers.title: Rhubarb extract attenuates periodontitis by modulating an MMP3-associated inflammatory-ferroptotic axis: Integrated multi-omics analysis and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by dysregulated host immunity, oxidative injury, connective tissue breakdown, and alveolar bone loss. Rhubarb (Rhei Radix et Rhizoma) has anti-inflammatory and redox-modulating properties, but its therapeutic mechanism in periodontitis remains unclear.
papers.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
papers.summary: This study shows that rhubarb extract can reduce periodontitis severity by targeting an MMP3-associated inflammatory-ferroptotic axis, as revealed by integrated multi-omics analysis and experimental validation. The findings suggest a new therapeutic mechanism for rhubarb in treating periodontal disease.

papers.title: A Bayesian Approach to Interpret Time-Resolved Experiments Using Molecular Simulations.
papers.abstract: Time-resolved experiments can provide unique insights into dynamic processes such as protein folding, ligand binding, and many other molecular processes. These experiments are, however, difficult to interpret at the molecular level because they generally report on signals that are averaged over multiple configurational states and because they often report on processes that are well beyond what can be studied using most simulation methods. Here, we describe an approach to use molecular simulations to model and interpret time-resolved experiments. The method, which we term trBME (time-resolved B
papers.summary: This paper introduces trBME, a Bayesian method that uses molecular simulations to interpret time-resolved experiments, which are often difficult to analyze due to signal averaging over multiple molecular states. The approach helps bridge the gap between experimental data and molecular-level dynamics, such as protein folding or ligand binding.

papers.title: System-Size Effects on the Molecular Dynamics Simulation of an All-Aromatic Liquid Crystal.
papers.abstract: Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations are presented for a prototypical all-aromatic calamitic liquid crystal that has recently emerged as a benchmark system for testing theories of nematic order. By performing simulations with progressively larger systems, up to an unprecedented total of 12,600 molecules, we investigate the impact of system size on the structural and dynamic properties of the material in the nematic and smectic A mesophases. Our results demonstrate that using a number of molecules on the order of 104 not only improves statistical sampling, thereby reducing uncertainty in al
papers.summary: This study uses large-scale molecular dynamics simulations (up to 12,600 molecules) to show that system size significantly affects the accuracy of structural and dynamic property predictions for an all-aromatic liquid crystal. Using ~10,000 molecules improves statistical sampling and reduces uncertainty in key material properties.

papers.title: Identification of α6-Containing Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptors as the Primary Target of Nereistoxin Insecticides and Structural Basis of Channel Blockade.
papers.abstract: Nereistoxin (NTX) and its derivative insecticides cartap and monosultap have been used for decades to control lepidopteran pests by targeting nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs). Unlike neonicotinoid agonists that induce excitatory neurotoxicity, nereistoxin insecticides act as antagonists, blocking cholinergic neurotransmission. However, the molecular target and mechanism of action of these compounds remain incompletely understood. Here, we elucidated the mode of action of cartap and monosultap in Drosophila melanogaster through integrated genetic and computational approaches. Bioassay
papers.summary: This study identifies α6-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors as the primary target of nereistoxin insecticides (cartap and monosultap) in Drosophila, using genetic and computational methods. The insecticides act as antagonists, blocking cholinergic neurotransmission, which explains their distinct mode of action compared to neonicotinoid agonists.

papers.title: An Underactuated Omnidirectional Docking Mechanism for Modular Serpentine Robots with DNA-Inspired Helical Continuum Units.
papers.abstract: Bio-inspired serpentine robots show strong potential for operation in unstructured environments, yet existing systems often lack reliable modular docking, adaptive grasping, and an effective balance between structural stiffness and motion dexterity. This study proposes a Modular Omnidirectional Serpentine Robot (MOSR) that integrates a DNA-inspired tendon-driven helical continuum unit, an underactuated omnidirectional spherical docking gripper, and adaptive gripper fingers within a single module. The helical continuum unit provides two-degree-of-freedom compliant bending while improving axial
papers.summary: This paper presents a modular serpentine robot design inspired by DNA, featuring a helical continuum unit for flexible bending and an underactuated spherical docking gripper for reliable connection between modules. The approach aims to improve the balance between structural stiffness and motion dexterity in bio-inspired robots for unstructured environments.

papers.title: Silver-Loaded Turbinaria turbinata Oil Nanoemulsions: Antimicrobial and Anticancer Potential Revealed Through In Vitro Assays and Molecular Docking.
papers.abstract: Nanoemulsions are promising nanotechnology-based delivery systems that may improve the stability, bioavailability, and cellular uptake of therapeutic agents. Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) have been reported to exhibit high antibacterial and anticancer activities via several mechanisms, such as the generation of oxidative stress and disruption of cellular membrane integrity. Breast cancer (MCF-7) and ovarian cancer (SK-OV-3) represent two highly aggressive malignancies that pose major global health challenges. Brown algae oil is a natural marine-derived product with a number of bioactive compoun
papers.summary: This study developed silver-loaded nanoemulsions from brown algae oil and tested their antimicrobial and anticancer effects in lab assays. The nanoemulsions showed activity against breast and ovarian cancer cells, with molecular docking suggesting potential mechanisms of action.

papers.title: From Atomic Channels to Deployable Membranes: A Design-Oriented Framework for Graphene Oxide Transport, Functionalization, and Scalability.
papers.abstract: Graphene oxide (GO) membranes present a compelling alternative to the permeability-selectivity trade-off inherent in conventional polymer membranes. However, the incomplete mechanistic understanding and the absence of scalable, defect-controlled fabrication processes continue to hinder their practical deployment. This review synthesizes and integrates transport mechanisms, computational modeling, fabrication, and translational constraints across graphene-based membrane architectures into a comprehensive design-oriented framework. Five key aspects of this synthesis are highlighted. Firstly, the
papers.summary: This review paper synthesizes current knowledge on graphene oxide membranes, covering transport mechanisms, computational modeling, fabrication methods, and scalability challenges. The authors propose a comprehensive design-oriented framework to address the gap between fundamental understanding and practical deployment of these membranes.

papers.title: Phylogenetic analysis of amino acid sequences indicates a central role of transmembrane domain structural elements in MHC class II function.
papers.abstract: Human leukocyte antigen class II genes are highly polymorphic. This raises the question of how polymorphisms are distributed across the entirety of the class II molecule and how this distribution affects function. We performed a comprehensive analysis of amino acid variability across the entire class II molecule, using class II amino acid sequences ranging from humans to ancient species such as cartilaginous fish. This analysis is unique in its scale and reveals that while the membrane distal antigen recognition domain exhibits a high frequency of amino acid variability, other domains exhibit
papers.summary: This study uses a large-scale phylogenetic analysis of MHC class II amino acid sequences across diverse species to map evolutionary variability across the entire molecule. The authors find that while the antigen-binding region is highly variable, specific structural elements in the transmembrane domain also show significant conservation and variation, suggesting they play a central functional role beyond simply anchoring the protein.

papers.title: SELEX-Based Aptamer Technologies for Toxin Analysis: Screening, Optimization, and Computational Assisted Design.
papers.abstract: The accurate and sensitive detection of toxin contamination remains a pressing challenge for food safety, environmental integrity, and public health, because conventional analytical methods suffer from high costs, poor field stability, and inadequate sensitivity for trace-level emerging contaminants. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of biosensor technologies for toxin detection, with a dedicated focus on nucleic acid aptamers and SELEX (Systematic Evolution of Ligands by Exponential Enrichment) technology. We systematically categorize nine SELEX variants developed for toxin
papers.summary: This review covers SELEX-based aptamer technologies for detecting toxins in food and the environment, categorizing nine SELEX variants and discussing optimization strategies including computational design. It highlights how aptamer-based biosensors can overcome limitations of conventional methods like high cost and poor sensitivity.

papers.title: The Marine-Derived Cyclopentapeptide Turnagainolide B Suppresses Melanoma via Autophagic Flux Disruption and Inhibits Tumorigenesis In Vivo.
papers.abstract: Melanoma remains highly lethal with frequent resistance to current therapies. Here we identify a marine-derived cyclopentapeptide, turnagainolide B, as a potent anti-melanoma agent that selectively kills B16-F10 melanoma cells (IC50 = 50 μM) with low toxicity to normal skin cells. Using bioassay-guided isolation, we also obtained a new analogue, turnagainolide H, and elucidated their structures and biosynthetic pathways. Mechanistically, turnagainolide B induces a previously undescribed "dual-hit" autophagic signature: it simultaneously promotes autophagy initiation (via PI3K/mTOR suppression,
papers.summary: A marine-derived compound, turnagainolide B, selectively kills melanoma cells by disrupting autophagy, and shows anti-tumor activity in mice. This study identifies a new mechanism of action for a potential melanoma therapy.

papers.title: Membrane Potential: Accuracy and Reproducibility of Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: The membrane dipole potential (Ψd) is a critical modulator of ion transport and protein function, making the ability to accurately predict its modifications essential for rational drug design and membrane biophysics. While molecular dynamics (MD) simulations offer a powerful alternative to challenging in vitro experiments, their predictive accuracy is often hampered by sensitivities to simulation setups and force field parameterization. In this study, we provide a systematic evaluation of how system composition, box size, water models, and small-molecule parameterization protocols influence th
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates how molecular dynamics simulation parameters (system composition, box size, water models, and small-molecule parameterization) affect the accuracy and reproducibility of membrane dipole potential predictions. The findings highlight key sources of variability that must be controlled to enable reliable computational predictions for drug design and membrane biophysics.

papers.title: Cathepsin B-Oriented Screening, Isolation, and Antitumor Validation of Bioactive Metabolites from Sargassum polycystum.
papers.abstract: Marine medicinal algae represent a valuable reservoir of bioactive metabolites for anticancer drug discovery, yet the efficient identification of target-relevant compounds from chemically complex marine matrices remains challenging. In this study, an integrated cathepsin B-oriented strategy was developed to discover, prioritize, isolate, and validate antitumor metabolites from the brown alga Sargassum polycystum. Affinity ultrafiltration LC-MS was first applied to screen CTSB-binding constituents from the crude extract, followed by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and gray rel
papers.summary: This study developed a cathepsin B-oriented screening strategy to identify and isolate antitumor metabolites from the brown alga Sargassum polycystum, combining affinity ultrafiltration LC-MS, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations. The approach successfully prioritized bioactive compounds from a complex marine extract, demonstrating a targeted method for anticancer drug discovery from marine algae.

papers.title: BoltzOmics: Predicting genetic variant effects on drug binding with Boltz-2.
papers.abstract: A mechanistic understanding of how genetic variants alter drug-receptor binding is central to precision medicine, drug response prediction, and drug development. Yet, experimental mutation-drug profiling remains slow and expensive, while existing computational approaches often trade accuracy for scalability. We developed BoltzOmics, an interactive, open-source platform that integrates Boltz-2, a deep learning model for biomolecular structure prediction, to rapidly assess mutation effects on drug binding. Starting from amino acid sequences, the workflow queries databases for genetic variants, g
papers.summary: BoltzOmics is an open-source platform that uses the deep learning model Boltz-2 to rapidly predict how genetic variants affect drug-receptor binding from amino acid sequences. This tool aims to accelerate precision medicine and drug development by providing a scalable and accurate alternative to slow experimental mutation-drug profiling.

papers.title: Structural Organization of the Nvj3-Mdm1 Complex Reveals a Conserved Lipid-Compatible Contact Site Module.
papers.abstract: Membrane contact sites are organized by protein assemblies that physically couple organelles and coordinate lipid metabolism, yet the structural principles that enable lipid exchange across these junctions remain poorly defined. At the nuclear-vacuolar junction (NVJ) in budding yeast, the tethering protein Mdm1 and its binding partner Nvj3 form a complex that regulates lipid metabolic pathways, but the structural features underlying their interaction have not been resolved. Here, we use AlphaFold-based complex prediction and comparative structural analysis to define the organization of Nvj3-Md
papers.summary: This study uses AlphaFold to predict the structure of the Nvj3-Mdm1 complex, which organizes membrane contact sites in yeast and regulates lipid metabolism. The findings reveal a conserved lipid-compatible contact site module, providing new structural insights into how protein assemblies coordinate lipid exchange between organelles.

papers.title: Translating viral genetic data to PRRSV-2 cross-neutralization using machine learning.
papers.abstract: Swine herd immunization through modified live vaccination or live virus inoculation is a core strategy for controlling porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS), one of the most economically important endemic diseases in the United States that is caused by PRRSV-2. While antigenically homologous PRRSV-2 viruses are expected to elicit better immunological cross-protection, questions remain as to how genetic similarity translates to the degree of cross-protection elicited between the immunizing strain and subsequent challenge virus. For PRRSV-2, virus neutralization (VN) assays are co
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to predict cross-neutralization between PRRSV-2 virus strains based on their genetic sequences, addressing a key challenge in swine vaccine development. By translating viral genetic data into immunological protection estimates, the approach could help optimize vaccine strain selection for better cross-protection against this economically important swine disease.

papers.title: Therapeutic assessment of Nerium oleander-derived exosome-like nanoparticles against triple-negative breast cancer: a preliminary in vitro and network pharmacology approach.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype lacking estrogen, progesterone, and HER2 receptors, which restricts targeted therapies and contributes to poor survival. Conventional chemotherapeutics such as doxorubicin and cisplatin show limited efficacy, significant toxicity, and resistance, underscoring the need for alternative strategies. Nerium oleander, a traditional medicinal plant, has demonstrated anticancer activity through leaf extracts; however, the role of exosome-like nanoparticles derived from its flowers (NELNs) remains unexplored.
papers.summary: This study explores exosome-like nanoparticles from Nerium oleander flowers as a potential treatment for triple-negative breast cancer, using lab experiments and computational network analysis. The nanoparticles showed anticancer activity in cell lines, suggesting a novel plant-derived therapeutic approach for this aggressive cancer subtype.

papers.title: Discovery of novel peptidomimetics against HSP90-HOP interactions towards improved cancer therapeutics using machine learning strategies.
papers.abstract: The HSP90-HOP interaction orchestrates transfer of client proteins from HSP70 to HSP90, promoting their conformational maturation and stabilisation and thereby sustaining oncogenic signalling. The study explores a promising alternative for cancer chemotherapy by targeting this interface rather than the traditional ATP-binding site, which may circumvent the toxicity associated with classical HSP90 inhibitors. Despite its therapeutic relevance, the HSP90-HOP interface remains underexplored, particularly in the context of structure-guided peptidomimetic inhibitors, highlighting a critical gap in
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to discover new peptidomimetic compounds that block the interaction between HSP90 and HOP proteins, a promising cancer drug target that may avoid the toxicity of current HSP90 inhibitors. By targeting this protein-protein interface instead of the traditional ATP-binding site, the approach offers a potentially safer strategy for disrupting cancer-promoting signaling pathways.

papers.title: Virtual screening of Kocuria oceani AT-1 metabolites as potential maize growth regulators under drought conditions using molecular docking and dynamics simulation.
papers.abstract: Maize is a vital cereal crop, severely affected by environmental factors and climate change. Among abiotic factors, drought stress is considered one of the most detrimental factors limiting plant growth and biomass production. However, the molecular basis of bacterial metabolite-mediated drought tolerance in cereal crops remains poorly understood. The current in silico study aimed to investigate the molecular interactions between Kocuria oceani AT-1 metabolites and the maize UGT706F8 protein, using molecular docking and dynamics simulation analyses. The molecular interactions between bacterial
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to predict how metabolites from the bacterium Kocuria oceani AT-1 might interact with a maize protein (UGT706F8) to help the plant tolerate drought stress. The findings suggest specific bacterial compounds could be promising candidates for developing drought-resistant maize, though these are purely in silico predictions requiring experimental validation.
